regions.merged_text: NOTE: With a tinge of fraternal humor, the following letter -- at once poetic, yet decidedly earnest -- will be found a relief for any color of the "blues" (in season). A missionary in the Philippines, Rev. Edward Casey, writes an elder brother, Rev. Maurice Casey, at the time in Yonkers, N. Y. The latter, having resumed studying after twenty years vacation continued with the younger and was ordained just a year before him. Then after eighteen years of pastoral and missionary work joined the Capuchin Order as Fr. Joachim. The "K" - "C" used as an example, is at the same time familiar to the brothers as an equivalent of Casey.

regions.merged_text: ( Father Solanus wrote this prologue to the rhyme-letter of Msgr. Edward Casey as a little explanation. Father Solanus had copies made by some of his friends, as he did at other times with certain interesting, inspirational letters which he found useful to give to people when it might benefit their state of mind. A copy of this rhyme-letter was for a long time in the Monastery Office in Detroit for people to read while waiting for Fr. Solanus. Appears on #1009 of Msgr. Edw. Casey's letters)
